A unique imaginary-axis crossing exists exactly for a>3p, and a stable large-|q| limit plus crossing transversality proves an iff, with both signs of q. The synchronous transverse two-by-two blocks have negative trace and positive determinant. The exact nonnegative identity for F(t)-8 gives sharpness and the exact bounded growth band. value.rationale: A synchronizing positive-real edge coefficient can support two additional *isolated* equilateral splay attractors through reactive competition. The universal sharp threshold |q|/p>2sqrt2 and a finite bounded beta-window address the central natural question of when all three regular rotating-wave branches coexist stably. This phase boundary distinguishes existence from transverse attraction and has clear dynamical relevance, rather than being an arbitrary finite computation.
